gloss: tea snack; refreshments served with tea

definitions.gloss: tea snack; refreshments served with tea; tea cake
definitions.explanation: A snack or sweet served alongside tea, typically Japanese tea. Traditionally refers to Japanese confections or pickles, but can include any light food served with tea.

examples.japanese: お{茶請|ちゃう}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{煎餅|せんべい}→煎餅：04958_senbei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: To serve rice crackers as a tea snack.
What would you like for tea snacks?

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧お{茶請|ちゃう}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{用意|ようい}して→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother always prepares homemade Japanese sweets as tea snacks.

notes:
Composed of ⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧ (tea, with honorific お) + {請|う}け (receiving, accompanying). Refers to the food served alongside tea when welcoming guests or during a tea break. The word reflects the Japanese custom of always pairing tea with a small snack.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{茶請|ちゃう}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to serve as a tea snack
- お{茶請|ちゃう}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}する→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧: to prepare tea snacks
- お{茶請|ちゃう}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to have as a tea snack

TYPICAL TEA SNACKS:
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧: Japanese confections
- ⟦{煎餅|せんべい}→煎餅：04958_senbei⟧: rice crackers
- ⟦{漬物|つけもの}→漬物：04938_tsukemono⟧: pickles
- ⟦{羊羹|ようかん}→羊羹：05002_youkan⟧: sweet bean jelly

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese homes, it is customary to serve tea with a small snack when guests visit. The type of snack varies by region and season.
